repo_notes.content: Self-hosted Rails engine (gem, MIT, fork of AnjanJ/rails_error_dashboard) for error tracking inside the host app: exceptions are captured with Ruby state (locals + receiver ivars via TracePoint(:raise)) and Rails runtime health (connection pool, Puma, jobs, GC, memory), all stored in the app's own database. Dashboard at /red.
CQRS architecture: Commands for writes (lib/rails_error_dashboard/commands/), Queries for reads (queries/), Services for algorithms (services/).
Host-app safety is rule zero: never raise in the capture path, never block requests, budget every operation, clean up Thread.current, always re-raise the original exception.

No Rails asset pipeline dependency: no Sprockets/Propshaft/app/assets/public serving — all CSS inline in the layout <style> block, all JS inline in <script>; Bootstrap JS/Chart.js/Highlight.js via CDN only. Layout is fully self-contained to work behind any proxy.

Storm protection is on by default: during error floods it progressively reduces captured context + DB work, keeps a per-minute exemplar, records a Storm History ledger, and reconciles exact occurrence counts.

Testing has two tiers: ~5,300 RSpec specs plus chaos tests (bin/pre-release-test) that build real Rails apps in /tmp and exercise production-mode capture end-to-end. Lefthook runs chaos tests pre-commit.
See CLAUDE.md for architecture rules, test tiers, style conventions (rails-omakase RuboCop, array brackets with inner spaces), and common gotchas.
